title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Team Beta incurs the highest labor cost, chat is the slowest channel by resolution time, and email tickets reopen at a rate 122% higher than chat. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention, and agent workload shows moderate concentration among 18 agents.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta has the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma at $5,911.44 and Alpha at $4,604.91. Beta accounts for the largest share of total labor spend.
Chat is the slowest channel with a mean resolution time of 82.2 minutes, followed by phone at 74.1 minutes and email at 71.7 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 15.2%, compared to 6.8% for chat. Email's reopen rate is 122.5% higher than chat's, representing a substantial increase in reopening risk for the email channel.
Nine tickets meet the high-cost (labor_cost ≥ $100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤ 2) criteria. Of these, 11.1% were reopened, flagging a small but operationally significant at-risk segment.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.3 minutes, indicating notable spread. Mean satisfaction (where recorded) is 4.14 out of 5, with 14 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
There are 18 distinct agents. The busiest single agent handled 16 tickets, representing 7.3% of all tickets, suggesting workload is reasonably distributed with no extreme concentration.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; results should be treated as provisional until the underlying data quality issues are investigated and resolved.
Fourteen tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random.
The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment contains only 9 tickets, making percentage-based conclusions (e.g., reopen rate) statistically fragile.
The analysis covers a single export snapshot with no time dimension, so trends over time cannot be assessed.
Agent identity relies on agent_id from a joined roster; any mismatches during the join could distort agent concentration metrics.
conclusion: Support operations are broadly functional, with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a healthy average satisfaction score of 4.14. However, email tickets reopen at more than twice the rate of chat tickets, Team Beta drives the largest share of labor cost, and a small high-cost, low-satisfaction cohort merits focused quality review. Given the pipeline validation failures, these findings should be confirmed once data quality issues are remediated.
